source.title: Event-Grounded Sparse Autoencoders for Vision-Language-Action Policies
source.authors: Xin Jin; A. Chatterjee; Pranav Kumar; R. Paleja

record.file_problem: none; full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study does not test superposition geometry, but it tests the causal usefulness of SAE features in VLA policies and argues that they are a sparse but imperfect intervention basis. Its results qualify claims that SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units: effects vary sharply by architecture and site, and some random features cause disruption comparable to ranked features.
record.gate_note: The paper uses the superposition account as motivation for SAEs, but does not test feature-over-capacity storage, sparsity-dependent geometry, feature importance, or one-dimensional directions. It does test SAE-feature interventions as evidence about their causal interpretability. Results cited from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study trains SAEs on VLA residual streams and reports closed-loop success when the SAE reconstruction replaces the hidden state (Hooked SR, Table 1). This directly tests whether the dictionary captures what the policy needs, the completeness part of V5. In OpenVLA the reconstruction does not. The single-feature ablation rows measure causal sensitivity of chosen features, not completeness, stability or canonicality.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that SAE features are a sparse but imperfect causal basis for VLAs. Effects depend on architecture and intervention site, single-feature edits cannot isolate causal variables, and binary SR is coarse. They also report that SAE reconstruction fidelity (FVE) does not predict closed-loop fidelity.
record.recipe_differences: Uses BatchTopK SAEs trained on VLA residual-stream activations and event-grounded feature ranking with closed-loop latent edits; it does not reproduce the original toy-model setup or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Strongly dependent on architecture/stream and layer or hook site; PG and action-expert interventions differ substantially, and OpenVLA resid_post and mlp_out effects differ. In the PG joint-dropout results, effects vary by layer and LIBERO suite.

fits_no_version.finding: Causal leverage of single SAE features differs sharply by stream. OpenVLA event-aligned features drop SR by 21 pp vs 1.3 pp for random features. PG features drop SR by ≤3 pp. AE features collapse SR to ~0, and random AE features also drop SR by up to 23 pp.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ablating individual SAE features has selective, behavior-specific causal effects on the model's output.

fits_no_version.finding: Joint dropout of 16 PG features is severe at layer 0 (LIBERO-Goal 8% SR) and a no-op at layer 16.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Causal sensitivity to SAE feature removal depends on layer depth.

record.problems: Binary success rate is a coarse behavioral measure; single-feature edits do not cleanly isolate causal variables; the authors report that AE random features can cause broad disruption. The main Table 3 results give no uncertainty estimates. Real-robot SAE intervention values are shown only in a figure and are not extracted as rows here.
record.rows_left_out: Not included: real-robot SAE suppression dose-response values in Figure 5, because the plot provides no textual numeric values; decoder-vector steering diagnostics in Table 9, which test a different fixed-vector intervention rather than the primary SAE latent-edit protocol; target/off-target specificity results in Table 8, which address task locality rather than completeness or canonicality. Also omitted other non-SAE results and cited findings.

untested.parts: Stability across seeds, dictionary sizes or checkpoints; canonicality, meaning whether different SAEs find the same features. No such comparison is made.
All: no toy models, geometry or sparsity transition.
All: no neuron polysemanticity or capacity analysis.
All: no test of alternative causes of polysemanticity.
All: systems are VLAs, and spread across neurons is not measured.

missing.what: FVE, alive fraction and Hooked SR per stream and layer. This is the completeness test: OpenVLA Hooked SR is 0.0/0.0/0.2/34.8% against a 68% raw baseline despite high FVE. π0.5 PG and AE Hooked SR is 95.8–97.8%.
Success-prediction probe: SAE codes score 0.79–0.93 balanced accuracy vs 0.89–0.98 for raw hidden states. The authors say the codes are 'not lossless'.
Target/off-target zero-out: target SR 0.641 vs off-target SR 0.631. Event-selected features are shared across tasks rather than task-specific units.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's verdicts rest on ablation rows that do not measure V5's properties. The real bearing on V5 is the Hooked-SR completeness result in Table 1, which has no rows. The verdicts above are therefore text-based. The study is not an original source. Superposition is cited only as motivation.

versions.untested_parts: No test of toy-model superposition, overlapping near-orthogonal directions, or sparsity-dependent transitions and geometry.
No test of neuron polysemanticity or competition for representational capacity.
The paper notes SAE features may be polysemantic, but does not test polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of polysemanticity.
The systems are VLAs, not LLMs; the study does not measure feature spread across neurons or SAE recovery of sparse LLM features.
Tests causal intervention usefulness, not completeness, stability across checkpoints, or canonicality as a full account of the model's representation.
No comparison of one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Tested VLA streams and intervention sites
reader_labels.reason: Causal effects vary substantially by stream and site: PG single-feature edits are generally near baseline, while AE edits often collapse success and random AE features can also disrupt behavior; OpenVLA effects differ between resid_post and mlp_out (r01-r36, r53-r54). This qualifies the use of SAE features as clean, canonical causal units, without establishing completeness or stability.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Joint removal of 16 PG features across LIBERO suites and layers
reader_labels.reason: Joint interventions have markedly different effects by layer and suite, including little or no effect at later layers and severe losses at layer 0; this shows causal usefulness is conditional on intervention site and task (r37-r52).
